data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Adrasteia was the name of the goddess of the Furies and the avenger of vengeance. She was the one who meted out punishment to those who had wronged others, and her power was invoked to seek vengeance on behalf of the aggrieved. The name Adrasteia carries the meaning “Ruler of the Furies” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Adrasteia usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the furies and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Adrasteia represents strength, protection, and vengeance. She embodies the power to stand up for what is right and to seek justice for those who have been wronged. Her spiritual essence is one of courage, resilience, and determination, and she is a powerful guardian and protector for those who call upon her.
data.etymology: Adrasteia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the Furies.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adrasteia total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Although the name "Adrasteia" originally derives from Greek mythology, it has been adopted and used in the Christian tradition as a name for the Virgin Mary. In this context, Adrasteia is seen as the one who avenges the wrongs done against her son, Jesus Christ, and metes out divine punishment on those who seek to harm Him and His Church.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Adrasteia reminds us of the fierce determination and unwavering commitment of the Blessed Virgin Mary to protect and defend her Son, Jesus Christ, against all threats. It is a reminder of her powerful intercession on behalf of her children, and the assurance that she seeks justice and vengeance against those who harm us or our faith. At the same time, it is a call for us to follow in her example of courage and resolve in the face of opposition and adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adrasteia represents the unyielding, fearless aspect of divine justice. Her name evokes the power to confront and vanquish adversity, embodying the courage and strength needed to uphold moral righteousness.
